name: hcapp_getProfilePhotoUploadToken
description: Validates auth and returns the userId so the calling Azure Function can construct a scoped SAS write token for the profile-photos blob container. No side effects — pure auth check. The simplest of the photo SPs: no additional parameters, no kennel lookup, no extra validation beyond auth.

parameters.name: deviceId
parameters.description: Registered device UUID. Passed to HC6.ValidateAppAuth for auth resolution.

parameters.name: accessToken
parameters.description: Short-lived auth token validated against DeviceSecret.

rowsets.name: Envelope
rowsets.description: On auth failure: success=0, errorCode and errorType set. On success: success=1, plus userId. Note: on success the envelope and the userId are combined in a single rowset rather than split across two rowsets — this is an unusual shape for this SP family.

columns.name: userId
columns.description: HC.Hasher.id of the authenticated user. NULL on failure.

rowsets.description: Returned only on auth failure (paired with success=0 in rowset 0). Not present on success.

codeSmells.issue: Success rowset combines envelope and data in a single rowset
codeSmells.detail: On success, this SP returns SELECT 1 AS success, @userId AS userId — mixing the envelope (success flag) and the payload (userId) into one rowset. All other photo SPs in this family return the envelope at rowset 0 and payload at rowset 1. The inconsistency means the API shim and Dart caller must handle a different shape for this SP alone.
The SP has no TRY/CATCH block. An unexpected DB error will propagate as a raw SQL error rather than a structured error rowset. Low risk for a read-only SP with no DB writes.

breakingChanges: New SP — no HC5 predecessor. No breaking changes from migration.
